body: Emirates is one of the largest long-haul airlines in the world, with an all-widebody fleet of over 250 aircraft. It currently operates the Airbus A350-900, with 30 examples in service and 43 remaining on order, for a total of 73. Yet it also holds orders for over 200 Boeing 777X aircraft: 35 777-8s and 235 777-9s, for a total of 270. The A350-900 is the smallest aircraft Emirates operates today, while the 777-9 is the largest model of the 777X family and the largest airliner currently in production. Emirates also holds orders for 35 Boeing 787s.

The 777X order actually predates the current A350 order. Emirates was one of the initial customers for the Boeing 777X, ordering 150 examples at the 2013 Dubai Airshow, and it has grown its orderbook to 270 examples today. Its A350 history is more tangled: Emirates first ordered the A350-900 at the Dubai Airshow in 2007, with initial deliveries scheduled for 2014, but it canceled that order in 2014 and did not order A350s again until 2019. That order came as part of an agreement to cancel Airbus A380s, under which Emirates agreed to drop its remaining A380 orders and convert them to 40 A330-900s and 30 A350-900s, later changing the A330s to more A350s.

The reason for the heavy 777-9 commitment is Emirates' business model. The airline has built its entire business around moving high volumes of passengers through its hub in Dubai, mastering economies of scale to achieve lower unit costs. Dubai Airport is constrained, so the only practical way for Emirates to significantly grow its network is to move from the 777-300ER to the 777-9; going with more A350s would require maintaining the same capacity with the A350-1000 or downgrading with the A350-900. The 777-9's extra seats compared with the 777-300ER make it a natural fit, and as the closest match to the A380 today, it is the best available replacement for the superjumbo, which is expected to remain in service until the 2040s even as the fleet shrinks over time.

The 777X was also designed with Emirates, Etihad and Qatar Airways in mind, and its General Electric GE9X engines matter most for the Middle Eastern carriers: they are the largest turbofan engines ever made, producing over 134,000 lbs of thrust during testing while rated to produce 110,000 lbs in service, so the engine is not very stressed, which is important for reliability and durability. Emirates, meanwhile, has expressed reservations about the durability of the Rolls-Royce Trent XWB-97 engines on the competing A350-1000. In the end, the A350 is essentially for niche markets in Emirates' network, used for growth and to serve more marginal routes economically, while the 777X will become the mainstay of the fleet, replacing the 777-300ER fleet and likely at least part of the A380 fleet.
en.summary: Emirates operates just 73 A350s against 270 Boeing 777X orders. The 777-9's size fits the Dubai hub's scale economics and will replace the 777-300ER and eventually the A380, while the A350 serves smaller markets and new routes.
en.title: Why Emirates bet on the Boeing 777X instead of more Airbus A350s

body: 阿聯酋航空是全球最大的長程航空公司之一，機隊逾250架且全為廣體客機。現役空中巴士A350-900共30架、另有43架待交付，總計73架；但波音777X訂單卻逾200架：777-8共35架、777-9共235架，合計270架。A350-900是阿聯酋航空現役最小的機型，而777-9是777X家族中最大的型號，也是目前生產中最大的客機；阿聯酋航空另持有35架波音787訂單。

777X訂單其實早於現行的A350訂單。阿聯酋航空是波音777X的初始客戶之一，2013年杜拜航展訂購150架，訂單其後增至270架。A350的歷程則較曲折：阿聯酋航空2007年杜拜航展首度訂購A350-900、原訂2014年交付，2014年取消訂單，直到2019年才再度訂購；當時是配合取消空中巴士A380訂單的協議，阿聯酋航空同意放棄剩餘A380訂單、改訂40架A330-900與30架A350-900，後來又將A330改為更多A350。

重押777-9的原因在於阿聯酋航空的營運模式：以杜拜樞紐大量運送旅客，靠規模經濟壓低單位成本。杜拜機場容量受限，要大幅擴張航網，最實際的做法是從777-300ER換裝777-9；若增購A350，則須以A350-1000維持運量、或以A350-900降低運量。777-9比777-300ER多出的座位正合所需，也是目前最接近A380運量的選擇，A380機隊預計服役至2040年代，機隊規模雖將逐漸縮小，777X仍是最合適的接替者。

777X的設計亦考量阿聯酋航空、阿提哈德航空與卡達航空的需求，其中通用電氣GE9X發動機對中東業者最為關鍵：它是歷來最大的渦扇發動機，測試推力逾13.4萬磅、服役額定推力11萬磅，發動機負荷較低，有利可靠度與耐用度。相較之下，阿聯酋航空對競爭機型A350-1000所用的勞斯萊斯Trent XWB-97發動機耐用度有所保留。整體而言，A350在阿聯酋航空航網中主攻利基市場、以較低成本拓展邊際航線，777X則將成為機隊主力，接替777-300ER機隊、並可能接替部分A380機隊。
zh.summary: 阿聯酋航空A350機隊僅73架，777X訂單卻達270架。777-9的大運量契合杜拜樞紐規模經濟，是接替777-300ER與A380的主力；A350則主攻較小市場與新航線。
zh.title: 阿聯酋航空為何重押波音777X、而非增購空中巴士A350？
